fields.explanation: The original Z4 diagonal code C={(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)} and standard Gray map are preserved. The complete stored source explicitly defines the dot-product orthogonal complement and states the converse for every Z4 code, without the length72 or TypeII restrictions used in its later application. Mathlib ZMod4 and ZMod2 provide the rings; both codes are actual Submodule objects. The Gray image is proved equal to the binary submodule with repeated coordinate pairs, and that submodule is proved equal to its Mathlib orthogonalBilin complement under dotProductBilin. C is not equal to its quaternary complement because the original (1,1) has self-dot product2. These assertions use actual linear codes, not manually axiomatized arithmetic or vector surrogates.
fields.flaw: If the Gray image of a linear code over Z/4Z is binary self-dual, then the original quaternary code is self-dual.

0083 | \begin{abstract}
0084 | We prove that a putative $[72,36,16]$ code is not the image of linear code over $\ZZ_4$, $\FF_2 + u \FF_2$ or $\FF_2+v\FF_2$, thus proving that the extremal doubly-even $[72,36,16]$ binary code cannot have an automorphism group containing a fixed point free involution. Combining this with the previously proved result by Bouyuklieva that such a code cannot have an automorphism group containing an involution with fixed points, we conclude that the automorphism group of the $[72,36,16]$ code cannot be of even order, leaving $1$, $3$ and $5$ as the only possibilities.
0085 | \end{abstract}
0086 | 
0087 | 
0088 | \section{Introduction}
0089 | A long standing open problem asks whether a binary $[72,36,16]$ Type~II code exists, where Type~II indicates that the code is self-dual and the Hamming weight of all vectors in the code are congruent to $0 \pmod{4}.$  The question has remained open over 40 years and is the first in  a series of open questions about the existence of $[24k,12k,4k+4]$ Type~II codes. A number of attempts have been made to solve this problem, many of which have led to restrictions about the automorphism group of such a code if it exists. We can refer the reader to such works as \cite{Bouyuklieva}, \cite{Boyuklieva-2}, \cite{Nebe}, \cite{OBrien}, \cite{Yankov} and the references therein. The latest works indicate that the automorphism group of a doubly-even $[72,36,16]$ code has order $5$ or divides $24$.
0090 | 
0091 | Recently in \cite{Kier}, Kiermaier showed that the Gray image of a self-dual $\ZZ_4$ code cannot have parameters $(72, 2^{36},16)$.
fields.witness: Use the standard Gray map 0↦00, 1↦01, 2↦11, 3↦10. Let C=⟨(1,1)⟩≤Z₄²={(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)}. Its Gray image is {0000,0101,1111,1010}=span_F₂{0101,1010}. These two generators have zero self- and mutual binary dot products, so this dimension-2 code of length 4 is binary self-dual. But (1,1) belongs to C and its self-dot product is 1+1=2, not 0 in Z/4Z. Hence C is not self-orthogonal and cannot be quaternary self-dual.
